curriculum.curriculumText:
Computer Science

OBJECTIVES AND OUTPUT STANDARDS OF THE CURRICULUM



 Field of Study: Computer Science Disciplines:

 Discipline Code: 52480101

 Types of training: Formal

 Period of Training: 4.5 years

 Management Unit: The College of Information and Communications Technology - Can Tho University

 Department: Computer Science

 1. Training Objectives

 - Training computer science engineers with extensive knowledge of computer science to apply their skills in real-world problems. After graduating, students will have a solid knowledge in one of the specialized subfields: Intelligent systems, Machine learning & Data mining, Graphics & Computer vision, Safety & security information, and Modeling & system evaluation . Students will have ability to develop their thinking from theory to the reality of building intelligent systems, and capability of applying research into practice as well as the ability to participate in research projects and develop the field of computer science.

 2. Output Standard for Training Program

 After completing the training program, students will have the knowledge, skills and attitudes as follows:

 2.1.Knowledge

 2.1.1.Knowledge of general education

 - Having general foundational knowledge of theory of Marxism, Leninism and Ho Chi Minh's Ideology, knowledge of social science and humanism, physical education and National Defense Education.

 - Grasping the basic scientific knowledge and mathematics to serve in computer science: Mathematical analysis, Linear Algebra, Discrete mathematics, Probability and Statistics.

 2.1.2.Special basic knowledge

 - Basic knowledge of applied mathematics in computer science

 - Basic knowledge of computing theory: possibilities and limitations of the computer.

 - Basic knowledge of the role of computer science in information technology, knowledge of computer architecture, operating systems and computer networks.

 - Basic knowledge of database, database management systems, information systems, knowledge of analyzing, designing and building an information system for organizations and businesses.

 - Basic knowledge of software technology.

 - Intensive knowledge of data structures, algorithms and programming techniques including: structured, object-oriented and logic programming

 2.1.3.Specialized knowledge

 - Having a solid understanding in one of the specialized subfields: intelligent systems (artificial intelligence, data mining, machine learning); exploring multimedia data (computer graphics – image processing –computer vision); Safety & security information, and Modeling & system evaluation

 - Having programming skills, and knowledge of software development process

 2.2. Skills

 2.2.1.Hard skills

 - Applying the knowledge of mathematics and basic science in the field of computer science

 - Using graphics software, image processing, from simple to complex.

 - Having programming skills, the ability to develop from theory to practice, for example, building the intelligent system, and the ability to apply research into practice.

 - Reading, writing, presenting and defending ideas; skills of reading specialized documentation and communicating in a foreign language.

 - Having creative thinking, and critical thinking.

 2.2.2.Soft skills

 Teamwork: forming groups to work effectively; group operation; group development; team leader, having ability to work cooperatively.

 2.2.3. Attitudes

 Having positive attitudes in work, having morality and responsibility in work. Professional working style

 2.2.4. Position of learner after graduation

 - Students have chances working in: Consultant Company- Design the resolutions for information technology; manufacturing company, outsourcing services, software development and maintenance company; university, college, Research and Technology Transfer Institute belonging to computer science

 - Students after graduation can work in the positions as: programming, analyzing and designing, and testing software

 2.2.5. Study Opportunities, enhancement of education level after graduation

 - Build up self-learning and self-updating skill, creativity in work and lifetime learning habit

 - Build up the professional researching skills in computer science and relevant fields

 - Meet the learning requirements at different levels of posgraduate in field of computer Science and relevant fields

curriculum.curriculumText:
Information Systems

PROGRAM OBJECTIVES AND LEARNING OUTCOMES

 Field of study : Information Systems Code : 52480104

 Program Delivery Mode: Full time Time of study : 4 . 5 years

 Faculty : Information and Communication Technology

 Department : Information Systems

 1. Program objectives

 After graduating with a degree of Engineering in Information Systems, students can achieve excellent personal ethics, good logic thought, and necessary specialist knowledge in information technology as well as in other related fields (e.g., economics and management) to become experts in Information Systems in different environments such as in education, government, and enterprises.

 2. Learning outcomes

 Students are able to achieve the following knowledge, skills and behaviors:

 2.1. Knowledge

 2.1.1.General knowledge

 - General knowledge about Marx-Lenin, Vietnam Communist, Ho Chi Minh thought, and national defense education.

 - General knowledge about law, society and human science, health, and contemporary issues.

 - Basic knowledge about mathematics and natural science to acquire professional knowledge and to study in higher education levels.

 - Basic knowledge about usinga foreign language (English/French) at level A

 - Basic knowledge about computer, office and other common software.

 2.1.2.Basic knowledge

 - Basic knowledge about solutions in information systems safety and solutions in network security

 - Basic knowledge for consulting and designing the IT solutions for enterprises

 - I nterdisciplinary knowledge about enterprise information systems; knowledge in data mining and business intelligence for enterprises.

 2.1.3.Specialized knowledge

 - Specialized and interdisciplinary knowledge to build, develop, and administer several types of information systems such as MIS, GIS, DSS, e-commerce, and e-learning.

 - Specialized knowledgeabout information systems development process

 - Specialized knowledgeabout information systems analysis and design

 - Specialized knowledgeabout system integrations

 2.2. Skills

 2.2.1.Hard skills

 - Applying new and modern techniques for building and developing information systems

 - Using relational database management systems, geographic information systems, as well as tools/software in information systems analysis and design

 - Collecting, specifying, and testing user requirements.

 2.2.2. Soft skills

 - Presenting ideas; writing reports; and defending proposal/project

 - Building and working in groups; managing team/members; organizing/coordinating tasks; and deploying the information systems

 - Communicating at a common level using English/French language. Reading and understanding specialized documents written in English/French

 2.3. Behaviors

 - Being self-confident, enthusiastic, passionate and adaptability to the changes.Understanding professional and ethical responsibility

 - Forming the professional working style

 - Being proactive in developing individual career

 - Being self-study and lifelong learning

 2.4. Job positions

 - Being a Programmer in software companies

 - Being an Expert/Specialist in consulting, designing and developing IT solutions for enterprises

 - Being an Expert/Specialist in information systems analysis and design in software companies

 - Being a Lecturer in College/University

 2.5. Research and lifelong learning

 - Having ability in advanced research in information systems and other related fields

 - Having ability in leaning graduate/post-graduate levels in Information Systems and other related fields

 2.6. References

 Heikki Topi, Joseph S. Valacich, Ryan T. Wright, Kate M. Kaiser, J.F. Nunamaker, Jr. Janice C. Sipior, and G.J. de Vreede. 2010. Curriculum Guidelines for Undergraduate Degree Programs in Information Systems. Association for Computing Machinery (ACM)

Information Systems

PROGRAM OBJECTIVES AND LEARNING OUTCOMES

 Field of study : Information Systems Code : 52480104

 Program Delivery Mode: Full time Time of study : 4 . 5 years

 Faculty : Information and Communication Technology

 Department : Information Systems

 1. Program objectives

 After graduating with a degree of Engineering in Information Systems, students can achieve excellent personal ethics, good logic thought, and necessary specialist knowledge in information technology as well as in other related fields (e.g., economics and management) to become experts in Information Systems in different environments such as in education, government, and enterprises.

 2. Learning outcomes

 Students are able to achieve the following knowledge, skills and behaviors:

 2.1. Knowledge

 2.1.1.General knowledge

 - General knowledge about Marx-Lenin, Vietnam Communist, Ho Chi Minh thought, and national defense education.

 - General knowledge about law, society and human science, health, and contemporary issues.

 - Basic knowledge about mathematics and natural science to acquire professional knowledge and to study in higher education levels.

 - Basic knowledge about usinga foreign language (English/French) at level A

 - Basic knowledge about computer, office and other common software.

 2.1.2.Basic knowledge

 - Basic knowledge about solutions in information systems safety and solutions in network security

 - Basic knowledge for consulting and designing the IT solutions for enterprises

 - I nterdisciplinary knowledge about enterprise information systems; knowledge in data mining and business intelligence for enterprises.

 2.1.3.Specialized knowledge

 - Specialized and interdisciplinary knowledge to build, develop, and administer several types of information systems such as MIS, GIS, DSS, e-commerce, and e-learning.

 - Specialized knowledgeabout information systems development process

 - Specialized knowledgeabout information systems analysis and design

 - Specialized knowledgeabout system integrations

 2.2. Skills

 2.2.1.Hard skills

 - Applying new and modern techniques for building and developing information systems

 - Using relational database management systems, geographic information systems, as well as tools/software in information systems analysis and design

 - Collecting, specifying, and testing user requirements.

 2.2.2. Soft skills

 - Presenting ideas; writing reports; and defending proposal/project

 - Building and working in groups; managing team/members; organizing/coordinating tasks; and deploying the information systems

 - Communicating at a common level using English/French language. Reading and understanding specialized documents written in English/French

 2.3. Behaviors

 - Being self-confident, enthusiastic, passionate and adaptability to the changes.Understanding professional and ethical responsibility

 - Forming the professional working style

 - Being proactive in developing individual career

 - Being self-study and lifelong learning

 2.4. Job positions

 - Being a Programmer in software companies

 - Being an Expert/Specialist in consulting, designing and developing IT solutions for enterprises

 - Being an Expert/Specialist in information systems analysis and design in software companies

 - Being a Lecturer in College/University

 2.5. Research and lifelong learning

 - Having ability in advanced research in information systems and other related fields

 - Having ability in leaning graduate/post-graduate levels in Information Systems and other related fields

 2.6. References

curriculum.curriculumText:
BACHELOR OF BUSINESS IN BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION
International University - Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City (VNUHCM)
Duration: 4 years | Total Credits: 139 | Language: English
Accreditation: AUN-QA (2012, 2017), ACBSP (2023)

========================================
PROGRAM STRUCTURE
========================================

SEMESTER 1 (Year 1)
- Writing AE1 (2 credits)
- Listening AE1 (2 credits)
- Introduction to Business Administration (3 credits)
- Introduction to Micro Economics (3 credits)
- Business Computing Skills (3 credits)
- Financial Accounting (3 credits)
- Physical Training 1 (3 credits)
- Philosophy of Marxism and Leninism (3 credits)

SEMESTER 2 (Year 1)
- Writing AE2 (4 credits)
- Listening AE2 (4 credits)
- Math for Business (4 credits)
- Introduction to Macro Economics (3 credits)
- Principles of Management (3 credits)
- Political economics of Marxism and Leninism (2 credits)
- Physical Training 2 (3 credits)

SEMESTER 3 (Year 2)
- Scientific socialism (2 credits)
- Critical Thinking (3 credits)
- Principles of Marketing (3 credits)
- Statistics for Business (3 credits)
- General Law (3 credits)
- History of Vietnamese Communist Party (2 credits)
- Elective: Introduction to Sociology (3 credits) or Introduction to Psychology (3 credits)

SEMESTER 4 (Year 2)
- Workshop 1 (3 credits)
- Organizational Behavior (3 credits)
- International Economics (3 credits)
- Quantitative Methods for Business (3 credits)
- Fundamental of Financial Management (3 credits)
- Ho Chi Minh's Thoughts (2 credits)
- Elective: Vietnamese History and Culture (3 credits) or World Economic Geography (3 credits)

========================================
SPECIALIZATION ORIENTATIONS (Year 3-4)
========================================

Students choose one of four orientations:

--- ORIENTATION 1: BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION ---
Required Courses:
- Business Ethics (3 credits)
- Business Law (3 credits)
- Strategy Formulation and Implementation (3 credits)
- Production and Operations Management (3 credits)
- Quality Management (3 credits)
- Business Communication (3 credits)
- Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management (3 credits)
- Human Resources Management (3 credits)
- Logistic and Supply Chain Management (3 credits)
- Project Management (3 credits)
- Business Research Methods (3 credits)
- Workshop 2 Business Management (2 credits)
- Internship (3 credits)
- Specialized Internship (3 credits)
- Thesis (12 credits)

Elective Courses:
- E-Commerce (3 credits)
- Management Information Systems (3 credits)
- Sales Management (3 credits)
- Customer Service Management (3 credits)
- International Financial Management (3 credits)
- Leadership (3 credits)
- Business Game (3 credits)
- Special Study (3 credits)
- International Business Management (3 credits)
- Organizational Design and Change (3 credits)
- Negotiation and Relationship Management (3 credits)
- Risk Management (3 credits)
- Franchising (3 credits)

--- ORIENTATION 2: INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS ---
Required Courses:
- Business Ethics (3 credits)
- Business Law (3 credits)
- Strategy Formulation and Implementation (3 credits)
- Import Export Management (3 credits)
- International Marketing (3 credits)
- Business Communication (3 credits)
- Business Research Methods (3 credits)
- Internship (3 credits)
- Specialized Internship (3 credits)
- Workshop 2 on International Business (2 credits)
- Thesis (12 credits)

Elective Courses:
- E-Commerce (3 credits)
- Management Information Systems (3 credits)
- Corporate Finance (3 credits)
- Brand Management (3 credits)
- Global Strategic Management (3 credits)
- International Business Law (3 credits)
- International Financial Management (3 credits)
- Corporate Governance (3 credits)
- Multicultural Management (3 credits)
- International Business Management (3 credits)
- Negotiation and Relationship Management (3 credits)
- Risk Management (3 credits)

--- ORIENTATION 3: MARKETING ---
Required Courses:
- Business Ethics (3 credits)
- Business Law (3 credits)
- Strategy Formulation and Implementation (3 credits)
- Marketing Research (3 credits)
- Consumer Behavior (3 credits)
- Marketing Strategy (3 credits)
- Business Communication (3 credits)
- Business Research Methods (3 credits)
- Internship (3 credits)
- Specialized Internship (3 credits)
- Workshop 2 on Marketing (2 credits)
- Thesis (12 credits)

Elective Courses:
- E-Commerce (3 credits)
- Management Information Systems (3 credits)
- Advertising and PR (3 credits)
- B2B Marketing (3 credits)
- Retail Management (3 credits)
- Customer Relationship Management (3 credits)
- Marketing Channels (3 credits)
- New Product Planning (3 credits)
- Interactive Marketing (3 credits)
- Brand Management (3 credits)
- Sales Management (3 credits)

--- ORIENTATION 4: HOSPITALITY ---
Required Courses:
- Business Ethics (3 credits)
- Business Law (3 credits)
- Introduction to Hospitality Industry (3 credits)
- Food and Beverage Management (3 credits)
- Leadership and Management Skills in Hospitality Management (3 credits)
- Legal issues in the Hotel and Restaurant Management industry (3 credits)
- Housekeeping Operations & Management (3 credits)
- The Professional Waiter (3 credits)
- Front Office Management and Operation (3 credits)
- Hotel Management and Operation (3 credits)
- Hospitality Sales and Marketing (3 credits)
- Workshop 2 on Hospitality Management (2 credits)
- Internship (3 credits)
- Specialized Internship (3 credits)
- Thesis (12 credits)

Elective Courses:
- Hospitality Facilities Management (3 credits)
- Quality Management in the Hospitality (3 credits)
- Safety, Sanitation and Security (3 credits)
- Service Management (3 credits)
- Supervision in the Hospitality (3 credits)
- Revenue Management (3 credits)
- Cruise Line Operation and Management (3 credits)
- Resort Management and Development (3 credits)
- Conference and Event Management (3 credits)
- Food and Beverage Cost Control (3 credits)

Shared Workshop & Elective Courses:
- Workshop 2 on Financial (2 credits)
- Workshop 2 on Accounting Issues (2 credits)
- Geographical Information System (3 credits)

========================================
KEY COURSE DESCRIPTIONS
========================================

Introduction to Business Administration: Provides a comprehensive overview of the business environment, including the nature and purpose of business, forms of business ownership, management functions, marketing, finance, and human resources. Students gain foundational knowledge of how organizations operate in local and global markets.

Principles of Management: Covers the fundamental concepts and theories of management including planning, organizing, leading, and controlling. Students learn about organizational structures, decision-making processes, and leadership styles applicable in modern business contexts.

Principles of Marketing: Introduces the core concepts of marketing including market segmentation, targeting, positioning, the marketing mix (product, price, place, promotion), and consumer behavior analysis. Students develop skills in creating basic marketing strategies.

Financial Accounting: Covers the fundamentals of financial accounting including the accounting cycle, preparation and analysis of financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement), and basic accounting principles and standards.

Statistics for Business: Introduces statistical methods and their application in business decision-making, including descriptive statistics, probability distributions, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and data interpretation for managerial insights.

Organizational Behavior: Examines individual and group behavior within organizations, covering topics such as motivation theories, team dynamics, leadership, organizational culture, communication, and change management.

Strategy Formulation and Implementation: Focuses on strategic management processes including environmental analysis, competitive strategy formulation, strategic planning, and implementation. Students learn to analyze industry structures, competitive advantages, and develop strategic plans for organizations.

Production and Operations Management: Covers the principles and techniques of managing production and operations systems, including capacity planning, inventory management, quality control, process design, and supply chain optimization.

Business Research Methods: Equips students with skills in designing and conducting business research, including research design, data collection methods, quantitative and qualitative analysis, and research report writing.

Human Resources Management: Covers key aspects of managing human resources including recruitment, selection, training and development, performance management, compensation, and employee relations within organizations.

International Marketing: Examines marketing strategies and practices in the international business environment, including market entry strategies, cross-cultural marketing, global branding, and adaptation vs. standardization decisions.

Consumer Behavior: Studies the psychological, social, and cultural factors that influence consumer purchasing decisions. Topics include perception, motivation, attitudes, decision-making processes, and their implications for marketing strategy.

Introduction to Hospitality Industry: Provides an overview of the hospitality industry including hotels, restaurants, tourism, and event management. Students learn about industry structure, career opportunities, and current trends in hospitality management.

Hotel Management and Operation: Covers the operational and managerial aspects of running a hotel, including front office, housekeeping, food and beverage, revenue management, and guest service excellence.

name: Biomedical Engineering
summary:
This program trains engineers capable of applying engineering principles, biological sciences, and medical knowledge to design, develop, operate, and evaluate healthcare technologies and systems.
The curriculum is technology-oriented, focusing on biomedical devices, biosignal processing, medical imaging, sensors, and healthcare systems, rather than clinical medicine.

curriculum.curriculumText:
SCHOOL OF BIOTECHNOLOGY - BIOTECHNOLOGY PROGRAM

Name of qualification: Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology
Official duration: 4 years, 137 credits
Language of instruction: English
Assessment/Accreditation: AUN-QA assessment in 2011 & 2017, ASIIN accreditation in 2023

COURSE LIST:

1st Year - Semester 1:
MA001IU Calculus 1 (4 credits), BT311IU Biology (3 credits), BT312IU Practice in Biology (1 credit), BT362IU Chemistry for Engineering (3 credits), EN007IU Writing AE1 (2 credits), EN008IU Listening AE1 (2 credits), PT001IU Physical Training 1 (3 credits)

1st Year - Semester 2:
PE021IU General Law (3 credits), PH058IU Physics for Biology (2 credits), EN011IU Writing AE2 (2 credits), EN012IU Speaking AE2 (2 credits), PE008IU Critical Thinking (3 credits), BT150IU Introduction to Biotechnology (2 credits), PT002IU Physical Training 2 (3 credits)

1st Year - Semester 3:
PE015IU Philosophy of Marxism and Leninism (3 credits), PE016IU Political Economics of Marxism and Leninism (2 credits), PE014IU Environmental Science (3 credits)

2nd Year - Semester 1:
BT313IU Genetics (3 credits), BT314IU Practice in Genetics (1 credit), BT010IU Plant Physiology (3 credits), BT315IU Analytical Chemistry (3 credits), BT316IU Practice in Analytical Chemistry (1 credit), PE017IU Scientific Socialism (2 credits)

2nd Year - Semester 2:
BT317IU Biostatistics (2 credits), BT318IU Practice in Biostatistics (1 credit), BT319IU Biochemistry (3 credits), BT320IU Practice in Biochemistry (1 credit), BT321IU Microbiology (3 credits), BT322IU Practice in Microbiology (1 credit), BT009IU Cell Biology (3 credits), BT210IU Human Physiology (3 credits)

3rd Year - Semester 1:
PE018IU History of Vietnamese Communist Party (2 credits), PE019IU Ho Chi Minh's Thoughts (2 credits), BT333IU Molecular Biotechnology (3 credits), BT334IU Practice in Molecular Biotechnology (1 credit), BT335IU Immunology (3 credits), BT336IU Practice in Immunology (1 credit)
Elective group 2 (min 12 credits): Plant Science, Developmental Biology, Scientific Writing Workshop, Human Pharmacology, Protein Biotechnology, Molecular Genetics, Molecular Microbiology, Microbial Genomic

3rd Year - Semester 2:
BT341IU Bioprocess Engineering (3 credits), BT342IU Practice in Bioprocess Engineering (1 credit), BT337IU Bioinformatics (3 credits), BT338IU Practice in Bioinformatics (1 credit)
Elective group 1 (6 credits): Project Management, Introduction to Business Administration, Business Communications, Principle of Marketing

3rd Year - Semester 2 (continued):
BT221IU Internship (2 credits)

4th Year - Semester 1:
BT216IU Experimental Design (3 credits)
Elective specialization courses: Medical Genetics, Crop Biotechnology, Techniques in Plant Biotechnology, Pharmaceutical Biotechnology, Molecular Diagnostics, Reproductive and Regenerative Biomedicine, Stem Cell Biology, Medical Microbiology, Microbial Biotechnology (each with practice components)

4th Year - Semester 2:
BT179IU Thesis (12 credits)

COURSE DESCRIPTIONS:
Biology (BT311IU): Covers biochemistry, molecular biology, cell biology, genetics, evolution, and ecology. Basic principles include chemical basis of life, cell theory, energy flow, gene expression, evolution by natural selection, and ecological interactions.
Practice in Biology (BT312IU): Demonstrates basic practice works with biological samples including cell observation, osmosis, enzyme reactions, photosynthesis, and cell division.
Chemistry for Engineering (BT362IU): Introduces basic chemistry principles for engineering students including measurements, matter states, atomic structure, chemical bonds, reaction types and rates, equilibrium, and thermodynamics.
Introduction to Biotechnology (BT150IU): Introduces fundamental concepts and applications of modern biotechnology.
Genetics (BT313IU): Covers principles of heredity, gene structure and function, genetic mapping, and population genetics.
Biostatistics (BT317IU): Statistical methods applied to biological and health sciences data analysis.
Biochemistry (BT319IU): Study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.
Microbiology (BT321IU): Study of microorganisms including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and their roles in biotechnology.
Cell Biology (BT009IU): Study of cell structure, function, and cellular processes.
Human Physiology (BT210IU): Study of the functions of the human body and its organ systems.
Molecular Biotechnology (BT333IU): Advanced techniques in recombinant DNA technology and molecular cloning.
Immunology (BT335IU): Study of the immune system, immune responses, and immunological techniques.
Bioprocess Engineering (BT341IU): Engineering principles applied to biological systems for production of useful products.
Bioinformatics (BT337IU): Computational methods for analyzing biological data including genomics and proteomics.
Experimental Design (BT216IU): Statistical design of experiments for biological research.

Total: 137 credits

=== COURSE DESCRIPTIONS ===

Introduction to Electrical Engineering: Introduces fundamental concepts of the electrical engineering profession including basic circuit analysis, electronic components, and an overview of the major sub-disciplines within electrical engineering.

Signals & Systems: Covers the fundamentals of signals and systems, including continuous-time and discrete-time signal representation, linear time-invariant systems analysis, Fourier series, Fourier transform, Laplace transform, and Z-transform.

Electronics Devices: Covers the fundamentals of semiconductor devices including p-n junction diodes, bipolar junction transistors (BJTs), and metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs). Topics include device physics, terminal characteristics, and circuit models.

Digital Signal Processing: Covers basic principles and applications of digital signal processing (DSP), including discrete-time signals and systems, the discrete Fourier transform (DFT), fast Fourier transform (FFT), and FIR/IIR digital filter design.

Electromagnetic Theory: Covers Maxwell's equations, potential functions, and transmission line theory. Topics include electrostatics, magnetostatics, time-varying fields, electromagnetic wave propagation, and guided wave structures.

Micro-processing Systems: Covers fundamentals of microprocessors and microcontrollers, including architecture, instruction sets, assembly language programming, interfacing with peripheral devices, and interrupt handling.

Principles of Communication Systems: Covers basic analog and digital communication system theory, including amplitude modulation (AM), frequency modulation (FM), pulse-code modulation (PCM), digital modulation schemes, and noise analysis in communication systems.

Digital Logic Design: Covers combinational and sequential digital logic circuits, including Boolean algebra, logic gates, multiplexers, decoders, flip-flops, registers, counters, and finite state machines.

Programming for Engineers: Covers programming in C language for engineering problem solving, including data types, control structures, functions, arrays, pointers, file I/O, and algorithmic thinking for engineering applications.

Machine learning and Artificial Intelligence: Covers machine learning techniques for engineering applications, including supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, classification, regression, clustering, and practical implementation for signal processing and telecommunications problems.

VLSI Design: Covers digital VLSI chip design based on CMOS technology, including CMOS logic design, layout techniques, design verification, timing analysis, and introduction to hardware description languages (HDL) for synthesis.

curriculum.curriculumText:
SCHOOL OF INDUSTRIAL ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT - LOGISTICS AND SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT PROGRAM

Name of qualification: Engineer in Logistics and Supply Chain Management
Official duration: 4 years, 150 credits
Language of instruction: English
Assessment/Accreditation: AUN-QA assessment in 2021

Three orientations: General, LSCM for E-Commerce, Supply Chain Analytics

GENERAL ORIENTATION COURSE LIST:

1st Year - Semester 1:
EN008IU Listening AE1 (2), MA001IU Calculus 1 (4), PH013IU Physics 1 (2), PH014IU Physics 2 (2), CH011IU Chemistry for Engineers (3), CH012IU Chemistry Laboratory (1), PT001IU Physical Training 1 (3)

1st Year - Semester 2:
EN011IU Writing AE2 (2), EN012IU Speaking AE2 (2), MA003IU Calculus 2 (4), PE008IU Critical Thinking (3), PH015IU Physics 3 (3), PT002IU Physical Training 2 (3), IS056IU Introduction to Logistics & SCM (1)

1st Year - Semester 3:
PE015IU Philosophy of Marxism and Leninism (3), PE016IU Political Economics (2)

2nd Year - Semester 1:
IS004IU Engineering Probability and Statistics (4), IS086IU Introduction to Computing (3), PE021IU General Law (3), MA027IU Applied Linear Algebra (2), IS019IU Production Management (3), IS055IU Principles of Logistics and SCM (3), PE017IU Scientific Socialism (2)

2nd Year - Semester 2:
IS020IU Engineering Economy (3), IS103IU Deterministic Models in OR (3), MA023IU Calculus 3 (4), IS057IU Warehouse Engineering Management (3), IS074IU Import-Export Management (3), PE018IU History of Communist Party (2), PE019IU Ho Chi Minh's Thoughts (2)

2nd Year - Semester 3: IS069IU Internship 1 (2), Military Training

3rd Year - Semester 1:
IS091IU MIS with ERP Applications (3), IS023IU Inventory Management (3), IS109IU Material Handling Systems (2), IS082IU Retail Management (3), IS110IU Procurement Management (2), IS104IU Time Series & Forecasting (2)
Elective group 01: Business Law / Systems Engineering (3)

3rd Year - Semester 2:
IS079IU Scientific Writing (2), IS027IU Scheduling & Sequencing (3), IS078IU Logistics Engineering & Supply Chain Design (3), IS065IU Supply Security and Risk Management (3), IS026IU Project Management (3), BA005IU Financial Accounting (3), IS105IU Cold Chain Systems (3)

3rd Year - Semester 3: IS070IU Internship 2 (3)

4th Year - Semester 1:
IS111IU Capstone 1 (3), IS067IU International Transportation & Logistics (3), IS033IU Multi-criteria Decision Making (3), IS062IU E-Logistics in SCM (3), IS107IU Supply Chain Modelling and Simulation (3)
Elective group 02: Quality Management, Sustainability in Supply Chain, Port Planning, Organizational Behavior, Leadership, Sales Management, Creative Thinking, Principles of Marketing, HR Management, Data Mining in Supply Chain, Decision Analytics (3)

4th Year - Semester 2:
For GPA > 70: IS071IU Thesis (10)
For GPA <= 70: IS094IU Advanced Industrial and Supply Chain Systems (4), IS108IU Capstone 2 (6)

LSCM FOR E-COMMERCE orientation: Replaces Cold Chain Systems with LSCM for E-Commerce Systems (3); Replaces Multi-criteria Decision Making with Decision Analytics (3)

SUPPLY CHAIN ANALYTICS orientation: Adds Data Collection Analysis and Applications (3) in Y3S1; Replaces Cold Chain with Predictive Data Analytics (3) in Y3S2; Replaces Supply Chain Modelling with Data Mining in Supply Chain (3) in Y4S1

COURSE DESCRIPTIONS:
Introduction to Logistics & SCM (IS056IU): Introduction to the field of logistics and supply chain management.
Principles of Logistics and SCM (IS055IU): Overview of fundamental concepts, business processes and models/tools combining SCM knowledge with analytical thinking.
Warehouse Engineering Management (IS057IU): Design and management of warehouse systems.
Import-Export Management (IS074IU): International trade procedures, documentation, and regulations.
Material Handling Systems (IS109IU): Design and analysis of material handling equipment and systems.
Procurement Management (IS110IU): Strategic sourcing, supplier management, and procurement processes.
Logistics Engineering & Supply Chain Design (IS078IU): Designing logistics networks and supply chain configurations.
Supply Security and Risk Management (IS065IU): Understanding and managing risks in supply chains.
International Transportation & Logistics (IS067IU): Global transportation modes, regulations, and logistics management.
Supply Chain Modelling and Simulation (IS107IU): Modeling and simulating supply chain systems for optimization.
Cold Chain Systems (IS105IU): Temperature-controlled supply chain management.

Total: 150 credits

curriculum.curriculumText:
Program: Applied Statistics
University: International University - VNUHCM
Official Source: https://hcmiu.edu.vn/en/academic-programs/undergraduate-programs/department-of-mathematics/
Degree Level: Bachelor

Program Objectives and Outcomes:
1. Award the Bachelor of Science in Statistics after 4 years and 139 credits
2. Provide rigorous training in statistical theory, data analytics, machine learning, and computational methods
3. Develop strong quantitative skills in probability, regression, Bayesian statistics, time series analysis, and multivariate methods
4. Prepare graduates for careers in data science, actuarial science, statistical consulting, business analytics, and quantitative research
5. Program has been internally assessed by the Center for Testing and Quality Assessment of Education, VNU-HCM in 2024
6. Deliver all instruction in English to prepare graduates for the global data analytics industry

DEPARTMENT OF MATHEMATICS - STATISTICS PROGRAM (APPLIED STATISTICS)

Name of qualification: Bachelor of Science in Statistics
Official duration: 4 years, 139 credits
Language of instruction: English
Assessment/Accreditation: Internally assessed by Center for Testing and Quality Assessment of Education, VNU-HCM in 2024

COURSE LIST:

1st Year - Semester 1:
EN007IU Writing AE1 (2), EN008IU Listening AE1 (2), PE021IU General Law (3), MAFE101IU Analysis 1 (4), MAFE109IU Introduction to Python (4), PE015IU Philosophy of Marxism and Leninism (3), PT001IU Physical Training 1 (3)

1st Year - Semester 2:
EN011IU Writing AE2 (2), EN012IU Speaking AE2 (2), MAFE103IU Analysis 2 (4), MAFE104IU Linear Algebra (4), IT069IU Object-Oriented Programming (4), MAFE212IU Financial Accounting (4), PE016IU Political Economics (2)

2nd Year - Semester 1:
MAFE201IU Real Analysis (4), MAFE203IU Analysis 3 (3), MAFE206IU Probability (3), MAFE204IU Database Management System (3), MAAS220IU Introduction to Statistics (2), PE017IU Scientific Socialism (2)

2nd Year - Semester 2:
MAFE316IU Statistics (4), MAAS221IU Introduction to Machine Learning (3), MAFE202IU Differential Equations (4), PE018IU History of Vietnamese Communist Party (2), BA115IU Introduction to Business Administration (3), PT002IU Physical Training 2 (3)

3rd Year - Semester 1:
MAAS318IU Stochastic Modeling (3), MAFE208IU Numerical Analysis (4), MAAS320IU Regression Models (3), PE019IU Ho Chi Minh's Thoughts (2), IT013IU Algorithms and Data Structures (4)
Elective group 1: Principles of Logistics and SCM / Financial Mathematics 1 / Financial Markets / Critical Thinking (3)

3rd Year - Semester 2:
MAFE303IU Optimization 1 (4), MAFE207IU Decision Making (3), MAAS322IU Statistical Computing (3), MAAS324IU Applied Time Series Analysis (3)
Elective group 2: Predictive Analytics / Supply Chain Security and Risk Management / Financial Risk Management 1 / Actuarial Mathematics for Life Contingent (3)

3rd Year - Semester 3: MAAS328IU Summer Internship (3)

4th Year - Semester 1:
IT157IU Deep Learning (4), MAAS410IU Bayesian Statistics (3), MAAS413IU Multivariate Statistical Analysis (3)
Elective group 3: Statistical Models for Actuarial Science / Statistical Methods for Finance / Data Mining in Supply Chain (3)
Elective group 4: Optimization 2 / Survey Sampling / Applied Probability Models in Actuarial Science (3)

4th Year - Semester 2: MAAS420IU Graduation Thesis (12)

COURSE DESCRIPTIONS:
Introduction to Statistics (MAAS220IU): Basic tools, language, and interpretation of statistics. Descriptive statistics, data visualization, measures of location/dispersion, exploratory data analysis, sampling methods.
Introduction to Machine Learning (MAAS221IU): Overview of machine learning fundamentals - problem types, model building, key algorithms.
Stochastic Modeling (MAAS318IU): Foundations in random processes including Markov property. Framework to formulate and analyze probabilistic systems.
Regression Models (MAAS320IU): Simple, multiple linear and nonlinear regression, OLS, inference, collinearity, model selection and validation.
Statistical Computing (MAAS322IU): Random variable generation, multivariate data visualization, Monte Carlo integration, bootstrap/jackknife, MCMC using R/Python.
Applied Time Series Analysis (MAAS324IU): Detrending, seasonal adjustment, smoothing, ARIMA, ARCH/GARCH models with software.
Predictive Analytics (MAAS325IU): Advanced statistical techniques for predictive modeling using R. Transition from theory to predictive analytics applications.
Actuarial Mathematics for Life Contingent (MAAS326IU): Probability models for life contingencies, life insurance and annuity analysis, premium determination.
Deep Learning (IT157IU): Capabilities, challenges, and consequences of deep learning for AI development.
Bayesian Statistics (MAAS410IU): Bayes rule, inference for single/multi-parameter models, hierarchical models, hypothesis testing, linear regression, MCMC methods.
Multivariate Statistical Analysis (MAAS413IU): Matrix algebra, multivariate distributions, estimation/testing, PCA, Copula theory, finance applications.
Statistical Models for Actuarial Science (MAAS411IU): Generalized linear models, non-linear models, Poisson regression with actuarial applications.
Statistical Methods for Finance (MAAS412IU): Quantitative methods and statistical techniques for finance using R/Python.
Survey Sampling (MAAS414IU): Sampling methods and techniques for practical survey problems.
Applied Probability Models in Actuarial Science (MAAS415IU): Probability models for property/casualty insurance, severity models, business problem solving.
Object-Oriented Programming (IT069IU): Basic to professional OOP design principles.
Algorithms and Data Structures (IT013IU): Introduction to data structures and algorithms including design, analysis, and implementation.

Total: 139 credits

DEPARTMENT OF MATHEMATICS - STATISTICS PROGRAM (APPLIED STATISTICS)

Name of qualification: Bachelor of Science in Statistics
Official duration: 4 years, 139 credits
Language of instruction: English
Assessment/Accreditation: Internally assessed by Center for Testing and Quality Assessment of Education, VNU-HCM in 2024

COURSE LIST:

1st Year - Semester 1:
EN007IU Writing AE1 (2), EN008IU Listening AE1 (2), PE021IU General Law (3), MAFE101IU Analysis 1 (4), MAFE109IU Introduction to Python (4), PE015IU Philosophy of Marxism and Leninism (3), PT001IU Physical Training 1 (3)

1st Year - Semester 2:
EN011IU Writing AE2 (2), EN012IU Speaking AE2 (2), MAFE103IU Analysis 2 (4), MAFE104IU Linear Algebra (4), IT069IU Object-Oriented Programming (4), MAFE212IU Financial Accounting (4), PE016IU Political Economics (2)

2nd Year - Semester 1:
MAFE201IU Real Analysis (4), MAFE203IU Analysis 3 (3), MAFE206IU Probability (3), MAFE204IU Database Management System (3), MAAS220IU Introduction to Statistics (2), PE017IU Scientific Socialism (2)

2nd Year - Semester 2:
MAFE316IU Statistics (4), MAAS221IU Introduction to Machine Learning (3), MAFE202IU Differential Equations (4), PE018IU History of Vietnamese Communist Party (2), BA115IU Introduction to Business Administration (3), PT002IU Physical Training 2 (3)

3rd Year - Semester 1:
MAAS318IU Stochastic Modeling (3), MAFE208IU Numerical Analysis (4), MAAS320IU Regression Models (3), PE019IU Ho Chi Minh's Thoughts (2), IT013IU Algorithms and Data Structures (4)
Elective group 1: Principles of Logistics and SCM / Financial Mathematics 1 / Financial Markets / Critical Thinking (3)

3rd Year - Semester 2:
MAFE303IU Optimization 1 (4), MAFE207IU Decision Making (3), MAAS322IU Statistical Computing (3), MAAS324IU Applied Time Series Analysis (3)
Elective group 2: Predictive Analytics / Supply Chain Security and Risk Management / Financial Risk Management 1 / Actuarial Mathematics for Life Contingent (3)

3rd Year - Semester 3: MAAS328IU Summer Internship (3)

4th Year - Semester 1:
IT157IU Deep Learning (4), MAAS410IU Bayesian Statistics (3), MAAS413IU Multivariate Statistical Analysis (3)
Elective group 3: Statistical Models for Actuarial Science / Statistical Methods for Finance / Data Mining in Supply Chain (3)
Elective group 4: Optimization 2 / Survey Sampling / Applied Probability Models in Actuarial Science (3)

4th Year - Semester 2: MAAS420IU Graduation Thesis (12)

COURSE DESCRIPTIONS:
Introduction to Statistics (MAAS220IU): Basic tools, language, and interpretation of statistics. Descriptive statistics, data visualization, measures of location/dispersion, exploratory data analysis, sampling methods.
Introduction to Machine Learning (MAAS221IU): Overview of machine learning fundamentals - problem types, model building, key algorithms.
Stochastic Modeling (MAAS318IU): Foundations in random processes including Markov property. Framework to formulate and analyze probabilistic systems.
Regression Models (MAAS320IU): Simple, multiple linear and nonlinear regression, OLS, inference, collinearity, model selection and validation.
Statistical Computing (MAAS322IU): Random variable generation, multivariate data visualization, Monte Carlo integration, bootstrap/jackknife, MCMC using R/Python.
Applied Time Series Analysis (MAAS324IU): Detrending, seasonal adjustment, smoothing, ARIMA, ARCH/GARCH models with software.
Predictive Analytics (MAAS325IU): Advanced statistical techniques for predictive modeling using R. Transition from theory to predictive analytics applications.
Actuarial Mathematics for Life Contingent (MAAS326IU): Probability models for life contingencies, life insurance and annuity analysis, premium determination.
Deep Learning (IT157IU): Capabilities, challenges, and consequences of deep learning for AI development.
Bayesian Statistics (MAAS410IU): Bayes rule, inference for single/multi-parameter models, hierarchical models, hypothesis testing, linear regression, MCMC methods.
Multivariate Statistical Analysis (MAAS413IU): Matrix algebra, multivariate distributions, estimation/testing, PCA, Copula theory, finance applications.
Statistical Models for Actuarial Science (MAAS411IU): Generalized linear models, non-linear models, Poisson regression with actuarial applications.
Statistical Methods for Finance (MAAS412IU): Quantitative methods and statistical techniques for finance using R/Python.
Survey Sampling (MAAS414IU): Sampling methods and techniques for practical survey problems.
Applied Probability Models in Actuarial Science (MAAS415IU): Probability models for property/casualty insurance, severity models, business problem solving.
Object-Oriented Programming (IT069IU): Basic to professional OOP design principles.
Algorithms and Data Structures (IT013IU): Introduction to data structures and algorithms including design, analysis, and implementation.

Total: 139 credits

 ELITECH PROGRAM 

 Human Higher Education Development Support Project on ICT (HEDSPI) 

 HEDSPI, part of the ELITECH training initiative, is recognized as the program with the highest average graduate salary among all information technology-related disciplines at Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST). Approximately 70% of HEDSPI graduates are employed in Japan, and today, the HEDSPI program has become a highly respected and reputable brand within the Japanese labor market. 

 

 

 

 

 
 
 
 
 Within the framework of the Human Higher Education Development Support Project on ICT (HEDSPI Project) – a collaborative initiative between the Governments of Vietnam and Japan, HUST launched the Vietnam–Japan Information Technology Engineer Program (commonly referred to as the HEDSPI Program) in 2006. The program aims to train information technology (IT) engineers whose qualifications are equivalent to those of graduates from Japanese universities. 

 Since 2021, the HEDSPI program has been restructured into an integrated training model. Upon completion of the bachelor’s phase, students may either graduate with a Bachelor’s degree or continue to pursue an Engineering or Master’s degree through an integrated academic pathway. 

 After graduation, HEDSPI students are well-positioned for employment in Japan, earning salaries comparable to those of Japanese IT graduates. In terms of Japanese language proficiency, students are taught directly by native Japanese instructors. Moreover, several specialized courses are delivered by professors and experts from leading Japanese universities and corporations. This ensures that students acquire the necessary language skills to work effectively in the Japanese professional environment. 

 SCHOLARSHIP OPPORTUNITIES AND FINANCIAL AID

 

 

 

 

 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 

 
 Scholarships and financial aid 

 In addition to the scholarships and financial aid provided by HUST, students enrolled in the HEDSPI Program with strong academic performance have the opportunity to receive merit-based scholarships from alumni foundations, information technology enterprise associations, or major corporations such as Microsoft, Samsung, Vingroup, VNPT, among others.

 Furthermore, students with strong teaching or research abilities may apply to serve as Teaching Assistants (TAs – supporting faculty in course instruction) or Research Assistants (RAs – collaborating with faculty on research projects conducted within the school’s network of laboratories). These positions offer a monthly stipend of up to 4 million VND, along with an official certificate issued by the university, which serves as a valuable credential for future applications to international scholarship programs. Currently, this is a unique initiative exclusively implemented by the university.

 For those pursuing the integrated Bachelor’s–Master’s program, students also have the opportunity to be awarded tuition reduction scholarships from the university, as well as postgraduate training scholarships sponsored by leading domestic and international corporations and organizations.

 Student exchange scholarships and internship opportunities 

 As part of the ELITECH Programs, the HEDSPI Program regularly invites lecturers who are professors from Japan and other countries to teach specialized courses to students. In addition, the collaboration with Japanese universities, such as the University of Aizu, Tokyo University of Technology, and others, provides students with opportunities for academic exchange and early exposure to Japanese-language working environments.

 Throughout their studies, students can also participate in internships at more than 200 partner enterprises, many of which are Japanese companies operating in Vietnam. These internships offer valuable hands-on experience in real-world professional settings, helping students bridge the gap between academic training and industry practice.

 

 

 

 

 
 
 
 
 STUDYING DURATION

 

 
 
 
 

 
 

 

 

 
 
 
 
 

- The HEDSPI Program offers two academic pathways: a four-year Bachelor’s program, and an integrated Bachelor’s–Master’s program lasting 5.5 years.

- In addition to its core objective of training students to attain a level of competence equivalent to that of IT graduates from Japanese universities, the HEDSPI program also provides students with the opportunity to pursue further study toward a Engineering degree or a Master’s degree. Moreover, graduates benefit from a wide range of academic advancement opportunities, including Master’s and Ph.D. programs at leading universities in Japan, as well as in other developed countries across Europe and North America.

 
 

 

 

 

 
 
 
 
 CONTENTS OF THE PROGRAM

 

 

 

 

 
 
 
 
 

- The curriculum of the HEDSPI Program is developed based on the expertise and experience of both Vietnamese and Japanese professors, and is aligned with Japan’s Information Technology Skill Standards (ITSS).

- ITSS Level 2.5 is set as one program outcome for HEDSPI IT graduates. With ITSS Level 2.5 and relevant experience, graduates are qualified to take on team leader roles (managing 3 to 5 members) in IT projects within the Japanese market.

- HEDSPI program offers two elective modules: 1) Artificial Intelligence and Big Data (AI and Big Data); 2) Artificial Intelligence and the Internet of Things (AIoT)

- Learning outcomes and details of the training program can be found here .

- In addition, students are also trained:
 

- Soft skills: Graduates are equipped with skills in presentation, teamwork, leadership, and other career-oriented competencies, preparing them to integrate successfully into the Japanese working environment and professional culture.

- Foreign languages: Japanese language training, including technical Japanese, is incorporated into the curriculum with the goal of ensuring that 100% of HEDSPI graduates achieve at least JLPT N3 proficiency. In practice, many students reach N2 level upon graduation, qualifying them to work directly in Japan.

 

 
 

 

 

 

 
 
 
 
 EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES

 

 

 

 

 
 
 
 
 100% of students have jobs after 1 year of graduation.

 Typical job positions: 

 

- Team Leader positions in major Japanese, American, or European corporations, particularly in the context of international IT projects.

- Bridge Engineer roles in leading Vietnamese companies serving the Japanese market.

- Approximately 70% of graduates secure employment with Japanese companies in Japan, with starting salaries ranging from 50 to 60 million VND per month, and in some exceptional cases, exceeding 100 million VND per month.

--- Full Curriculum Text ---
Bachelor of Laws (Luật) - Standard 4-year undergraduate program at Ton Duc Thang University, Faculty of Law.

Bachelor of Laws Program at Ton Duc Thang University aims to train law graduates with high political qualities, as well as good grounding knowledge about law, legal practice and other social aspects related to the legal field.

The Bachelor Program focuses on orienting students towards the ability to do scientific researches independently, as well as practical skills (such as critical thinking, team working, and self-study) to prepare for a career in law.

curriculum.curriculumText:
Program: Architecture
University: Ho Chi Minh City University of Architecture
Official Source: https://uah.edu.vn/dao-tao
Degree Level: Bachelor

Program Objectives and Outcomes:
1. Train architects with strong creative design abilities, technical knowledge, and understanding of cultural and environmental contexts
2. Develop skills in architectural design, urban planning, building construction systems, and sustainable design
3. Build competency in architectural representation through drawing, modeling, and digital tools (BIM, CAD, 3D visualization)

--- Full Curriculum Text ---
Bachelor of Architecture (Kiến trúc) - Standard program at Ho Chi Minh City University of Architecture (Trường Đại học Kiến trúc TP. Hồ Chí Minh - UAH), 196 Pasteur, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City.

UAH's educational philosophy is '5K' and the university motto is: 'Training autonomous, creative students who adapt to international trends'. Architecture is the university's flagship program, with an additional high-quality track (CT chất lượng cao) available.

The Architecture program trains students with strong creative design abilities combined with technical knowledge and understanding of cultural, environmental, and social contexts. The curriculum progresses through sequential architectural design studios of increasing complexity while building theoretical and technical foundations.

Core courses include: Architectural Design Studios (1-8, progressive complexity), History of Architecture (Vietnamese and World), Architectural Theory, Building Construction Technology, Structural Systems, Building Physics (Lighting, Acoustics, Thermal), Urban Design, Urban Planning, Landscape Architecture, Interior Architecture, Sustainable Architecture and Green Building, Architectural Representation, CAD, BIM, 3D Modeling, Construction Materials, Building Services Systems, Construction Management, Architecture Law and Regulations, and Professional Practice and Ethics.

The university offers related programs including: Architecture (standard and high-quality), Urban and Regional Planning (Qui hoạch vùng và đô thị), Landscape Architecture (Kiến trúc Cảnh quan), Interior Design (Thiết kế nội thất), Urban Arts (Mỹ thuật Đô thị), Construction Management (Quản lý xây dựng), and Infrastructure Engineering (Kỹ thuật cơ sở hạ tầng).

Graduates work as architects, urban designers, interior architects, project managers, construction consultants, BIM specialists, and sustainability consultants at architectural firms, construction companies, urban planning agencies, real estate development companies, and government planning departments.

Focus: Computer Science
Degree: Bachelor

1.5 Yêu cầu về môn học tài năng của chương trình
Trong chương trình Kỹ sư tài năng ngành An toàn Thông tin sinh viên được học các môn học tài năng trong các giảng viên đều có học vị Tiến sĩ, Phó Giáo sư, Giáo sư. Sinh viên theo học các môn tài năng sẽ được trang bị các kiến thức nâng cao, được tiếp cận các công nghệ tiên tiến và phương pháp nghiên cứu khoa học mới nhất. Các môn học tài năng sẽ được dạy với cơ sở vật chất đầy đủ và tốt nhất nên các sinh viên có điều kiện trao đổi chuyên môn với giảng viên được dễ dàng hơn, sinh viên được thực nghiệm nhiều hơn, được rèn luyện các kỹ năng như làm việc nhóm, kỹ năng giao tiếp. Đặc biệt với 2 môn “Đồ án chuyên ngành” và “Khóa luận tốt nghiệp”, sinh viên thực hiện dưới sự hướng dẫn của các giảng viên có trình độ Tiến sỹ trở lên và được thường xuyên tiếp xúc với các giảng viên được chọn lọc cả về chuyên môn lẫn đạo đức, được sinh hoạt trong các nhóm nghiên cứu nhỏ nên có điều kiện hơn trong việc rèn luyện và hoàn thiện khả năng nghiên cứu khoa học.

1.5 Yêu cầu về môn học tài năng của chương trình
Trong chương trình Kỹ sư tài năng ngành An toàn Thông tin sinh viên được học các môn học tài năng trong các giảng viên đều có học vị Tiến sĩ, Phó Giáo sư, Giáo sư. Sinh viên theo học các môn tài năng sẽ được trang bị các kiến thức nâng cao, được tiếp cận các công nghệ tiên tiến và phương pháp nghiên cứu khoa học mới nhất. Các môn học tài năng sẽ được dạy với cơ sở vật chất đầy đủ và tốt nhất nên các sinh viên có điều kiện trao đổi chuyên môn với giảng viên được dễ dàng hơn, sinh viên được thực nghiệm nhiều hơn, được rèn luyện các kỹ năng như làm việc nhóm, kỹ năng giao tiếp. Đặc biệt với 2 môn “Đồ án chuyên ngành” và “Khóa luận tốt nghiệp”, sinh viên thực hiện dưới sự hướng dẫn của các giảng viên có trình độ Tiến sỹ trở lên và được thường xuyên tiếp xúc với các giảng viên được chọn lọc cả về chuyên môn lẫn đạo đức, được sinh hoạt trong các nhóm nghiên cứu nhỏ nên có điều kiện hơn trong việc rèn luyện và hoàn thiện khả năng nghiên cứu khoa học.

1.5 Yêu cầu về môn học tài năng của chương trình
Trong chương trình Kỹ sư tài năng ngành An toàn Thông tin sinh viên được học các môn học tài năng trong các giảng viên đều có học vị Tiến sĩ, Phó Giáo sư, Giáo sư. Sinh viên theo học các môn tài năng sẽ được trang bị các kiến thức nâng cao, được tiếp cận các công nghệ tiên tiến và phương pháp nghiên cứu khoa học mới nhất. Các môn học tài năng sẽ được dạy với cơ sở vật chất đầy đủ và tốt nhất nên các sinh viên có điều kiện trao đổi chuyên môn với giảng viên được dễ dàng hơn, sinh viên được thực nghiệm nhiều hơn, được rèn luyện các kỹ năng như làm việc nhóm, kỹ năng giao tiếp. Đặc biệt với 2 môn “Đồ án chuyên ngành” và “Khóa luận tốt nghiệp”, sinh viên thực hiện dưới sự hướng dẫn của các giảng viên có trình độ Tiến sỹ trở lên và được thường xuyên tiếp xúc với các giảng viên được chọn lọc cả về chuyên môn lẫn đạo đức, được sinh hoạt trong các nhóm nghiên cứu nhỏ nên có điều kiện hơn trong việc rèn luyện và hoàn thiện khả năng nghiên cứu khoa học.

curriculum.curriculumText:
Information System at University of Information Technology - VNUHCM
Focus: Information Systems
Degree: Bachelor

Objectives:
1. Train IT professionals specialized in information systems analysis, design, and management
2. Provide solid foundation in database management, system analysis, and enterprise applications
3. Develop skills in web application development, data mining, and distributed databases
4. Equip students with knowledge of e-commerce, mobile application development, and business intelligence
5. Prepare graduates for careers as systems analysts, database administrators, and IT project managers
6. Foster research capabilities and lifelong learning in information systems field

curriculum.curriculumText:
Program: Information and Communication Technology (Double Degree with France)
University: University of Science and Technology of Hanoi
Official Source: https://usth.edu.vn/en/double-bachelors-degree-program-in-information-and-communication-technology-5541/
Degree Level: Bachelor

Program Objectives and Outcomes:
1. Provide foundation knowledge of computing and system administration, then professional knowledge of information systems, advanced databases, and project management
2. Focus on applied research and new technologies under two majors: Software Technology and Computer Science
3. Train students capable of working effectively in multidisciplinary teams and in an international environment
4. Prepare graduates for taking appropriate positions in the industry upon graduation and growing into leadership positions
5. Enable graduates to pursue scientific research or higher education
6. Emphasize critical thinking, self-learning, and practical skills through modern teaching methods
7. Award two Bachelor's degrees: one from USTH and one from a French partner university (Limoges, La Rochelle, or Lille)

Curriculum Structure and Representative Courses:

--- Full Curriculum Text ---
Double Bachelor's Degree Program in Information and Communication Technology (ICT). Total: 180 ECTS over 3 years.

Two majors: Software Technology and Computer Science.

Phase 1 (First 2 years at USTH): Taught in English by USTH lecturers (100% PhD holders). Covers computing fundamentals, system administration, information systems, advanced databases, and project management. Students also study French to achieve DELF B2 by end of Year 2.

Phase 2 (Final year at French partner university): Taught in French.

Partner universities for co-granting degree:
- University of Limoges (UNILIM) - top 7% worldwide, 15,000+ students, 29th in France
- University of La Rochelle - youngest multidisciplinary university in France (est. 1993), 6000+ students from 92 countries
- University of Lille - prestigious merger of 3 universities in 2018, renowned for IT and materials science research

Entry Requirements: Grade 11-12 average of at least 6.50/10 in Maths, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Informatics; IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 60 minimum; pass knowledge test and interview.

Note: Specific course-level curriculum not published on the program page. The program follows the Bologna Process.
